scope: Bounded primary/source-metadata checks for local notes, not an all-claim historical audit.

sources.title: International Phonetic Association, International Phonetic Alphabet, revised2020
sources.access: Official PDF downloaded to ignored working files; coordinator inspected the complete rendered page. Poppler emitted marked-content warnings, but the relevant labels and chart were legible.
sources.support: Clicks are classified as articulated consonants; the chart supplies no hierarchy of intellectual capacities.

sources.title: Glottolog, Telugu classification
sources.locator: Language search row telu1262/Telugu/Dravidian; language profile https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/telu1262
sources.access: Full search-result table and relevant profile sections read through web tool.
sources.support: Telugu belongs to the Dravidian family. This does not verify Carey’s cited preface or Humboldt’s claim about intelligibility.

sources.title: Open Library catalogue, Carey, A grammar of the Telinga language
sources.locator: Title/author; subjects: Telugu language Grammar; source record: Internet Archive grammaroftelinga00care
sources.access: Full relevant catalogue metadata read, not the book’s prefatory content. Follow-up LoC link returned an inaccessible redirect and was not retried.
sources.support: The historical Telinga title is catalogued as a grammar of Telugu; no claim to have checked the quoted preface.

sources.title: Whitney, Sanskrit Grammar, chapterII
sources.locator: §45(lingual/cerebral articulation),§87(Vedic accent marks),§§92–96(word accent and its limits)
sources.access: Relevant complete numbered paragraphs read in the primary-work transcription; no complete grammar reread or new print collation.
sources.support: The historical cerebral/lingual terminology describes tongue position; later scholarship documents Vedic accent. More than one accented syllable is discussed in§94, but this alone does not refute Humboldt’s narrower claim about two exactly equal accents.

sources.title: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Cantonese Flipped Classroom, Understanding Finals
sources.access: Complete relevant table and final examples read through web tool.
sources.support: Cantonese has syllabic nasals with tones, so a vowel-only statement is not valid as a general claim about all Chinese varieties. It does not identify exactly which varieties Humboldt’s sources described.
